title: A scaler that honours the estimator contract
hints: Keep `__init__` to plain assignments: `self.with_centering = with_centering` and so on. Why would converting `quantile_range` to a list there break `clone`?

`clone` rebuilds the estimator from `get_params()` and checks each parameter is the very object it passed in. Learned values go on attributes ending in `_`, set only in `fit`. `np.percentile(X, self.quantile_range, axis=0)` gives both percentiles at once. In `transform`, call `sklearn.utils.validation.check_is_fitted(self)` first.

fit: X = np.asarray(X, float); lo, hi = np.percentile(X, self.quantile_range, axis=0); self.center_ = np.median(X, axis=0) if self.with_centering else np.zeros(X.shape[1]); spread = hi - lo; self.scale_ = np.where(spread == 0, 1.0, spread); return self

misconceptions.init-does-work: An estimator's __init__ must only store its arguments, unchanged; validation and learning belong in fit, or clone and grid search break.
misconceptions.fit-returns-self: fit must return self so calls can be chained (`est.fit(X).transform(X)`) and pipelines can use it.
